pages.title: Meta-Architect Overview
pages.purpose: High-level introduction to Meta-Architect: what it is, why it exists, how it fits into the Codex ecosystem, and a map to all child pages covering the system in depth.

pages.title: Getting Started
pages.purpose: Step-by-step guide for installing Meta-Architect, bootstrapping a project, and running the first skill. Covers npm installation, `ma bootstrap`, `ma setup`, `ma doctor`, environment variables, and the CODEX_HOME layout.

pages.title: Core Concepts and Terminology
pages.purpose: Explains the foundational ideas that underpin the whole system: gated lanes, the fail-closed model, skills vs helper skills, the .ma runtime namespace, release state, and the kernel vs extension model.

pages.title: Skill System
pages.purpose: Overview of the Meta-Architect skill architecture: how skills are defined, installed, and invoked. Links to child pages covering the gated workflow skills, helper skills, and the $maestro umbrella manager.

pages.title: $maestro — Autonomous Manager
pages.purpose: Deep dive into the $maestro umbrella skill: how it inspects runtime state, chooses the next safe step, dispatches helper or gated work, manages the manager-run control plane, and handles team dispatch via the orchestrator.

pages.title: Gated Lane Skills
pages.purpose: Reference for each of the six gated skills ($arch, $sage, $flow, $vet, $vibe, $build): what each skill does, what status field it owns, its prerequisites, and its output artifacts.

pages.title: Helper Skills
pages.purpose: Reference for the four non-gating helper skills ($align, $diagnose, $tdd, $cleanup): their purpose, when to invoke them, and how they interact with the gated workflow without advancing release state.

pages.title: Skill Packaging and Installation
pages.purpose: Explains how skills are packaged into a tarball, installed into CODEX_HOME/skills, and mirrored into the plugin bundle. Covers skills-manifest, skills-validate, skills-pack, skills-install scripts and the postinstall lifecycle.

pages.title: CLI Reference (`ma`)
pages.purpose: Overview of the `ma` binary as the primary terminal interface. Links to child pages covering each command group and the Codex delegation mechanism.

pages.title: Setup and Diagnostic Commands
pages.purpose: Detailed reference for `ma setup`, `ma init`, `ma bootstrap`, `ma doctor`, `ma sdk-path`, and `ma skills`. Explains what each command creates, repairs, or reports.

pages.title: Workflow Commands
pages.purpose: Reference for `ma idea`, `ma status`, `ma run <skill>`, `ma merge`, and `ma release`. Explains the policy rules enforced by each command and how they update .ma/release.json.

pages.title: Codex Delegation and Launcher
pages.purpose: Explains how `ma` detects when arguments should be forwarded to the underlying Codex runtime, the `shouldDelegateToCodex` logic, the `MA_CODEX_BIN` environment variable, and the WSL codex-wrapper mechanism.

pages.title: Runtime Architecture
pages.purpose: Overview of the internal Node.js runtime that powers the skill execution engine. Links to child pages covering the state machine, subsystems, and the MCP client.

pages.title: Release State and Gate Enforcement
pages.purpose: Explains the release state machine: all status fields (idea_status through release_status), how they are stored in .ma/release.json, the build-gate evaluation logic, and the policy rules for merge and release promotion.

pages.title: Runtime Subsystems
pages.purpose: Covers the internal runtime subsystems seeded under .ma/state/: the maestro-manager (manager runs, dispatch plans, helper failure matrix), the orchestrator (task registry, mailbox, locks), workspaces, guidance stack, continuity notes, and signal hooks.

pages.title: MCP Live Client
pages.purpose: Deep dive into McpSseClient: the SSE connection lifecycle, JSON-RPC 2.0 request/response correlation, the endpoint discovery handshake, the 15-second timeout, and how $sage uses it to probe GitMCP endpoints.

pages.title: MCP and Evidence Configuration
pages.purpose: Overview of how Meta-Architect connects to external evidence sources via MCP. Links to child pages covering server configuration, local capabilities, and the discovery-to-verification workflow.

pages.title: MCP Server Configuration
pages.purpose: Explains mcp/servers.json, mcp/collections.json, mcp/fallback.json, and the GitMCP endpoint format. Covers how to add new evidence sources, the approved discovery accelerators, and the canonical $sage evidence order.

pages.title: Local Capabilities and Playbooks
pages.purpose: Covers mcp/local-capabilities.json, the first-party in-process capability registry (_state, memory, trace, team_run, code_intel, playbooks), and the native-playbooks.json / mcp/local/playbooks.js read-only playbooks contract.

pages.title: Plugin Bundle
pages.purpose: Overview of the plugins/meta-architect/ plugin bundle: its role as a mirror of the skills directory, the .codex-plugin/plugin.json manifest, .app.json, .mcp.json, and how the bundle is installed into the support bundle.

pages.title: Plugin Skill Definitions
pages.purpose: Reference for the SKILL.md files and openai.yaml agent configs inside plugins/meta-architect/skills/. Explains how plugin skills mirror the canonical skills/ directory and what the parity contract means.

pages.title: Codex Agent Definitions
pages.purpose: Covers the .codex/agents/ TOML files (Architect.toml, Sage.toml, Builder.toml, etc.) and .codex/prompts/ (enforcement.md, onboarding.md, release-rules.md, skill-contract.md) that configure Codex agent behavior for each skill role.

pages.title: Release Engineering
pages.purpose: Overview of the release pipeline: versioning, validation, Linux package builds, npm publication, and GitHub Actions workflows. Links to child pages for the release spec and CI/CD details.

pages.title: Release Specification and Lifecycle
pages.purpose: Detailed walkthrough of the release spec: versioning with npm version, the release:verify / release:check / release:assets pipeline, dist-tag discipline (latest, beta, next, canary), provenance requirements, and the QA readiness documents.

pages.title: Linux Native Packages
pages.purpose: Explains how .deb, .pkg.tar.xz, and .rpm packages are built from the npm package, the linux-package-lib.mjs / build-linux-packages.mjs scripts, the smoke test, and the dist/ artifact layout.

pages.title: GitHub Actions Workflows
pages.purpose: Reference for all CI/CD workflows: ci.yml (validate + linux-packages jobs), npm-publish.yml (provenance publish), release-sync.yml (automated PR on main push), release-advance.yml, pr-check.yml, codex-review.yml, and dependabot.

pages.title: Testing
pages.purpose: Overview of the test suite structure and testing philosophy. Links to child pages covering smoke tests, unit tests, and the policy/release-sync test helpers.

pages.title: CLI and Package Install Smoke Tests
pages.purpose: Explains the cli-smoke.test.js and package-install-smoke.test.js test files: what they verify (command routing, skill parity, .ma scaffold, MCP bootstrap), the fake-codex runtime pattern, and key environment variables used in tests.

pages.title: Policy and Release-Sync Tests
pages.purpose: Covers test/policy.test.js (validateReleaseOrigin, validateMergeTarget, canMarkBuildDone, rejectsDirectProdPromotion), test/release-sync.test.js, test/full-flow.test.js, and the temp-repo helper used in integration tests.

pages.title: Sprint Templates and Mission Examples
pages.purpose: Overview of the sprint/ lane templates and missions/ example scenarios. Links to child pages covering the sprint workflow documents and the bundled mission walkthroughs.
